# Sensitivity and sink-demand comparisons

<p>Sensitivity coverage is limited to explicit declarations. Undeclared content is not proven non-sensitive. Comparisons apply to the recorded processing and task-demand rules, not to all possible implementations. Completed input assessments identify removable ranges under the reviewed input contracts. A possible dependency is not evidence that sensitive plaintext is present.</p>

<details id="excerpt-6b86b273ff34fce19d6b"><summary>skill/SKILL.md lines 13–19</summary><pre>&quot;2.  **API Key:** Generate an API Key.\n3.  **Search Engine ID (CX):** Create a Programmable Search Engine at [cse.google.com](https://cse.google.com/cse/all), and get your CX ID.\n4.  **Environment:** Store your credentials in a `.env` file in your workspace:\n    ```\n    GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_key_here\n    GOOGLE_CSE_ID=your_cx_id_here\n    ```\n&quot;</pre></details>

<details id="excerpt-d4735e3a265e16eee03f"><summary>skill/scripts/search.py lines 27–27</summary><pre>&quot;    api_key = os.getenv(\&quot;GOOGLE_API_KEY\&quot;)\n&quot;</pre></details>

<details id="excerpt-4e07408562bedb8b60ce"><summary>skill/SKILL.md lines 14–19</summary><pre>&quot;3.  **Search Engine ID (CX):** Create a Programmable Search Engine at [cse.google.com](https://cse.google.com/cse/all), and get your CX ID.\n4.  **Environment:** Store your credentials in a `.env` file in your workspace:\n    ```\n    GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_key_here\n    GOOGLE_CSE_ID=your_cx_id_here\n    ```\n&quot;</pre></details>

<details id="excerpt-4b227777d4dd1fc61c6f"><summary>skill/scripts/search.py lines 28–28</summary><pre>&quot;    cse_id = os.getenv(\&quot;GOOGLE_CSE_ID\&quot;)\n&quot;</pre></details>

<details id="excerpt-ef2d127de37b942baad0"><summary>skill/scripts/search.py lines 6–14</summary><pre>&quot;def google_search(query, api_key, cse_id, num_results=5):\n    url = \&quot;https://www.googleapis.com/customsearch/v1\&quot;\n    params = {\n        &#x27;q&#x27;: query,\n        &#x27;key&#x27;: api_key,\n        &#x27;cx&#x27;: cse_id,\n        &#x27;num&#x27;: num_results\n    }\n    response = requests.get(url, params=params)\n&quot;</pre></details>

<details id="diagnostic-45f63d5d4595a67eda59"><summary>diagnostic_05967799b2104fd8c014</summary><pre>{
  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;diagnostic_05967799b2104fd8c014&quot;,
  &quot;code&quot;: &quot;processing_gap&quot;,
  &quot;reason&quot;: &quot;processing_gap_178f1c4655c450df1e50: The source establishes caught-object identity, then string conversion, prefix formatting and printing in order. String conversion can fail before exception_text or error_message exists; later failure can occur after one or both intermediate values exist. The retained record incorrectly computes both values before its protected alternatives. The supplied vocabulary cannot faithfully replace that record while covering all four CFG outputs: case-local values cannot escape through ordinary output bindings, one protected group provides only one return port, and separate protected groups cannot repeatedly bind the same handler_exception output. A single protected group also cannot be partitioned among the three independently declared rendering and delivery actions. Precise identity, formatting and delivery operations are individually available, but their required conditional output availability is not expressible with these ports and scoping rules. A placeholder would retain the same availability defect or conceal the known print effect. This limitation concerns representation, not unknown exception contents; the latter remain a separate interface precision limitation.&quot;,
  &quot;instruction_id&quot;: &quot;ir_063&quot;,
  &quot;operation_id&quot;: null,
  &quot;blocking&quot;: true,

}</pre></details>

<details id="diagnostic-ca3668317429fa666b4f"><summary>diagnostic_0a3e53c8b02e018cf670</summary><pre>{
  &quot;id&quot;: &quot;diagnostic_0a3e53c8b02e018cf670&quot;,
  &quot;code&quot;: &quot;processing_gap&quot;,
  &quot;reason&quot;: &quot;processing_gap_4f3e0fecda2d0955e2fc: The four bindings are fully known: inputs 1, 2, 3 and 4 map respectively to outputs 0, 1, 2 and 3. The remaining conflict is representational: this instruction transfers arguments into an already represented callee body, while its mandatory call-role validation requires a wire call. The supplied call operation introduces delivery and acquisition; the source establishes no additional acquisition returning these formal arguments. The actual HTTP interaction remains represented at ir_049. Output aliases precisely express the transfer but have already been rejected for this required role. A placeholder cannot satisfy that role either. Resolving this boundary requires support for an internal argument-transfer operation or correction of its role requirement; inventing another wire call would duplicate unsupported behavior.&quot;,
